abstract: Maintains dedicated exhibition power feed tie-ins and internal ambient noise assessments
system_message:
You are High-voltage utility coordinator (ELEC). You serve as the High-voltage utility coordinator (ELEC) for international exhibition pavilion venue selection. Your responsibilities include maintaining dedicated exhibition power feed tie-ins and internal ambient noise assessments, as well as tracking voltage total harmonic distortion across candidate venue facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Total harmonic distortion（HARM）
information_points.content:
ELEC-HARM-JSB：Power quality analyzer datalogs under simulated full load indicate Jurong Waterfront Pavilion Complex maintains a voltage total harmonic distortion of 3.2% across its secondary distribution transformers.
ELEC-HARM-QVD：According to secondary distribution transformer datalogs under simulated full load, Marina Bay Expo Center Hall A exhibits a voltage total harmonic distortion of 2.4%.
ELEC-HARM-O8L：For Changi Aerospace Exhibition Hub, secondary distribution transformer monitoring under simulated full load shows a voltage total harmonic distortion of 1.8%.

information_points.title: Maintains dedicated exhibition power feed tie-ins and internal ambient noise assessments（POW）
information_points.content:
ELEC-POW-RPJ：Jurong Waterfront Pavilion Complex does not possess dedicated high-voltage grid tie-in readiness, as verified at its on-site 22 kV step-down distribution substation where dual feeder lines from independent grid sectors are not operational. Baseline facility sound audits indicate a peak internal ambient noise floor of 46 dB within the main auditorium interior under standard quiet standby conditions.
ELEC-POW-6R6：For Marina Bay Expo Center Hall A, verification at the on-site 22 kV step-down distribution substation confirms that dedicated high-voltage grid tie-in readiness is true, with dual feeder lines from independent electrical grid sectors energized and operational. The peak internal ambient noise floor in the main auditorium interior is 50 dB during quiet standby mode with all primary electrical transformers and circulation fans running.
ELEC-POW-B3N：For Changi Aerospace Exhibition Hub, dedicated high-voltage grid tie-in readiness is true based on utility interconnect certification of its on-site 22 kV step-down substation having dual operational feeder lines. Baseline acoustic audits record a peak internal ambient noise floor of 46 dB in the main auditorium interior with primary transformers and circulation fans operating in quiet standby mode.
